questions.stem: Each side of a regular quadrilateral (square) is \(25\text{ mm}\) long. What is the total length (perimeter) of all the sides of the shape?
questions.hint: Convert to the same metric unit first if needed (1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m), then write the number sentence.

keyPoints.note: Check units carefully before adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing.

steps.explain: Recall that a regular quadrilateral (square) has 4 equal sides.
Multiply 4 sides by 25 mm per side (or add 25 + 25 + 25 + 25).
Check by doubling twice: 25 × 2 = 50, then 50 × 2 = 100 mm (which is 10 cm).
Therefore, the total length of all four sides is 100 mm.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the length of an ironing board?
questions.hint: Compare each unit with a 30 cm school ruler: 115 mm is only 11.5 cm (too short), and 115 m is longer than a football field (too long)!

keyPoints.note: Use benchmarks: 10 mm = 1 cm, a school ruler = 30 cm, 100 cm = 1 m.
Compare each unit with a 30 cm school ruler: 115 mm is only 11.5 cm (too short), and 115 m is longer than a football field (too long)!

steps.explain: Convert 115 mm to centimetres by dividing by 10: 115 mm = 11.5 cm, which is shorter than a pencil — far too small for an ironing board.

questions.stem: Tad had a one-metre length of string. He cut off \(30\text{ cm}\) to tie up a package. How much string did he have left?
questions.hint: Convert to the same metric unit first if needed (1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m), then write the number sentence.

keyPoints.note: Check units carefully before adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing.

steps.explain: Convert 1 metre into centimetres so both lengths share the same unit: 1 m = 100 cm.
Subtract the 30 cm cut off from 100 cm.
Check by adding back: 70 cm + 30 cm = 100 cm = 1 m.
Therefore, Tad had 70 cm of string left.

steps.explain: Convert 1 km into metres: 1 km = 1000 m.
Subtract the 600 m already walked from 1000 m.
Therefore, it is 400 m further to the bakery.

questions.stem: The length of the swimming pool is \(50\text{ m}\). Marie swims \(250\text{ metres}\) every morning. How many laps of the pool does she swim?

steps.explain: Divide the total distance swum (250 m) by the length of 1 lap (50 m).
